text.sdge:cc-dr-2026-04-01-evaluation|urpx:de: This filing models the standard Schedule DR customer only: the Base Services Charge of $0.79343 per day, the flat EECC generation rate of $0.18808 per kWh, the eight UDC components, DWR-BC and WF-NBC, and the $0.10701 per kWh Baseline Adjustment Credit that produces the Tier 1 rate. Four published provisions are not represented. The DR-MB columns on Sheet 2, whose total effective Medical Baseline rates for bundled customers are $0.31899 per kWh up to 130 percent of baseline and $0.40284 above it, with the Wildfire Non-Bypassable Charge and DWR Bond Charge shown as N/A for DR-MB on Sheet 4 and the standard Base Services Charge of $0.79343 per day; no SDG&E Medical Baseline overlay exists in this corpus, so that customer class cannot be billed from the data at all. The Franchise Fee Differential of 5.78 percent applied to monthly billings for customers inside the corporate limits of the City of San Diego. The Direct Access and Community Choice Aggregation bill path of General Special Condition 9.b, under which the EECC and DWR-BC components are credited back and the applicable Cost Responsibility Surcharge is added; the EECC that is modeled is the bundled rate, which per EECC Special Condition 6 and Sheet 2 note 1 already embeds the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment. And the semi-annual California Climate Credit of $49.36 under Schedule GHG-ARR named in the applicability section. Separately, the two service tiers are bounded at a dimensionless 1.3 standing for 130 percent of the customer's allowance, so the General Special Condition 3 allowance table itself (Basic Allowance 9.0, 10.4, 13.6 and 15.9 kWh per day in summer for the Coastal, Inland, Mountain and Desert zones and 9.2, 9.6, 12.9 and 10.9 in winter, with a separate All Electric set) is absent and a consumer must supply the customer's allowance to resolve the tier boundary. Three groups of provisions are out of scope rather than missing: the DR-CARE and DR-FERA columns and the DRAH and FERA Base Services Charges of $0.39688 per day are carried by separate overlay filings; General Special Conditions 1, 5, 6, 7 and 8 (load checks, standard lighting voltage, welder ratings, incidental farm service and common use service) are service-qualification and verification terms rather than rates; and EECC Special Conditions 2 to 5, carried into this schedule from the retired Schedule EECC, are service restrictions, a twelve-month term of service with a one-year return bar, early termination to a Direct Access provider or CCA, and TOU period grandfathering for non-residential customers, none of them a rate.

text.deferral:4: General Special Condition 9's enrollment cap is a term of availability of this schedule, stated twice in this filing's own PDF, and the model records neither statement. Sheet 1: "There is a cap of 10,000 customers who may take service on this rate, as defined in General Special Condition 10." The cap itself is General Special Condition 9 on Sheet 7; General Special Condition 10 is the Deed-Restricted Affordable Housing Requirement. General Special Condition 9 verbatim: "Enrollment Cap: There is a cap of 10,000 customers who may take service on this rate. A customer's ability to enroll will depend on availability. In the event that the cap is reached, SDG&E is not responsible for maintaining a queue of customers who want to take service on TOU-ELEC." The v0.5.1 ontology has no enrollment-cap property, so this is a blocked deferral.
